facts.statement: Ebrachosuchus was a basal phytosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in Bavaria, southern Germany.
facts.quote: Ebrachosuchus is an extinct genus of basal phytosaur known from the Late Triassic (late Carnian stage) of Bavaria, southern Germany.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Ebrachosuchus is a complete skull missing both lower jaws, designated as holotype BSPG 1931 X 501.
facts.quote: It is known only from the holotype BSPG 1931 X 501, a complete skull missing both mandibles.

facts.statement: The fossil was found at Ebrach Quarry in bed number 9 of the Blasensandstein Member of the Hassberge Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected at Ebrach Quarry, bed number 9 from the late Carnian-aged Blasensandstein Member of the Hassberge Formation.

facts.statement: Oskar Kuhn first named the genus Ebrachosuchus and its type species E. neukami in 1936.
facts.quote: It was first named by Oskar Kuhn in 1936 and the type species is Ebrachosuchus neukami.

facts.statement: Ebrachosuchus belongs to the parent group Parasuchidae.
Ebrachosuchus is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Ebrachosuchus is classified as a reptile.
Ebrachosuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Recent phylogenetic analysis re-validated the genus Ebrachosuchus by showing E. neukami is more closely related to Mystriosuchinae than to Paleorhinus.
rejected.quote: More recently, a phylogenetic analysis found E. neukami to be more closely related to Mystriosuchinae than to Paleorhinus and thus the genus Ebrachosuchus was re-validated.
